method: Synthesis of (1) audit_research.json MTFS data + (2) savings_recommendations.json strategic themes + (3) cross-sector benchmarks library (burnley-council/data/shared/savings_benchmarks_library.json) gated by council tier + PFI/ALMO/LATCo/audit-opinion flags. Each additional opportunity is verified as NOT in the council's existing programme.

context.audit_opinion: not located - audit certificate / opinion text not retrievable via WebSearch indexes; Audit Certificate 2023-24 + Auditor's Annual Report 2023-24 are listed as published on gateshead.gov.uk/article/3659

existing_programme.title: Agency / locum staff demand reduction (£2M concentrated)
existing_programme.rationale: £2M of agency-staff spend across 1 master vendors. Top: COMENSURA LTD (£2M). Standard transformation: cap agency premium at 20% above substantive rate, workforce-plan permanent conversion (6-9 month payback), regional bank pool, open-book master-vendor margins. CIPFA experience: 8-15% reduction in 12-18 months.

existing_programme.title: Energy procurement via CCS / LASER / NEPO frameworks (£43M baseline)
existing_programme.rationale: £43M utility spend across 3 suppliers. Top: EDF ENERGY (£30M), CORONA ENERGY LTD (£12M), NPOWER (£1M). Crown Commercial RM6306 + LASER / NEPO consortium flex purchase typically saves 4-8% vs direct supplier contracts on a 3-yr horizon. Plus solar PV self-generation on council estate (7-9 yr payback) + DESNZ Public Sector Decarbonisation Scheme grants up to 100% capex on heat pump conversion.

existing_programme.title: Treasury management + borrowing cost optimisation (CFR proxy £349M)
existing_programme.rationale: Annual revenue £437M implies indicative CFR c. £349M. Standard levers: internal borrowing from earmarked reserves, PWLB Certainty Rate trade, MMF counterparty restructuring, LGPS Property Investment Pool inclusion. 10-30bp saving on external debt typical from a fresh review.

existing_programme.title: LGPS employer contribution opportunity (2025 triennial valuation cycle)
existing_programme.rationale: Indicative pay bill £175M × c. 22% employer contribution rate = £38M annual employer contribution. Most LGPS funds materially over-funded post-2022 (returns 2022-25 averaged 7-10% pa vs 3-4% discount-rate assumption). 2025 triennial valuation typically yields 2-4pp employer-rate reduction over 2026-2029. Confirm with administering authority + actuary.

existing_programme.title: Fees, charges + traded-services income optimisation (£44M base)
existing_programme.rationale: Indicative fees & charges + traded-services income c. 10% of revenue = £44M. Standard levers: annual CPI uplift discipline, full-cost-recovery audit on discretionary services (parking, planning, licensing, sports, adult learning, property hire), commercial pricing on traded services. LGA experience: 5-15% income uplift sustainable over 2-3 years.

existing_programme.title: Insurance retention + premium review (£0.4M premium estimate)
existing_programme.rationale: Indicative insurance premium £0.4M (10bp of revenue). Standard 3-5 yr renewal cycle. Levers: tender via IPG / RM Partners (10-25% premium reduction typical), retention review (increase excess + build risk-fund reserve). London-borough cohort average 12% premium reduction at last tender.

existing_programme.title: Contracts Finder portfolio review (90 notices; 1 contracts at £10M+ ceiling)
existing_programme.rationale: Contracts Finder data: 90 notices (67 awarded, £41M aggregate ADVERTISED CEILING value, 0% SME). IMPORTANT: advertised contract value is a CEILING set to avoid retender risk under PCR 2015 Reg.72 / Procurement Act 2023 s.31 — actual spend through the awardee is typically 30-70% of ceiling, with some off-contract ledger spend permitted within the 50%/50% modification limits. 1 contracts at £10M+ ceiling totalling £16M (ceiling, NOT spend) — top 3: Contract for the Provision and Operation of a Material Recov (ceiling £16M). Matched against ledger: GB-Gateshead: TPPL Gateshead Council NEPO GM & — ceiling £0.0M, actual ledger spend with awardee £0.3M; GB-Gateshead: TPPL Gateshead Council NEPO GM & — ceiling £0.0M, actual ledger spend with awardee £3.8M; GB-Gateshead: TPPL Gateshead Council NEPO GM & — ceiling £0.2M, actual ledger spend with awardee £1.8M. Aggregate identified actual spend £644M. SME-awarded share 0% is below the Procurement Reform 2023 / PPN 03/24 ambition (33% SME share by value). Standard procurement-data savings levers (% of ACTUAL ledger spend, not ceiling): (a) modification-history scrutiny under PCR 2015 Reg.72, (b) Procurement Act 2023 s.31 contract change notice review, (c) re-tender benchmark vs CCS framework rates on next renewal. 2-8% on actual spend through major contracts is a defensible upper bound.

existing_programme.title: Companies House compliance follow-up (£108M flagged — 5 overdue, 2 dissolved, 3 insolvency-history)
existing_programme.rationale: Companies House lookup on top-50 suppliers identified £108M of spend with statutory-compliance flags: £58M to suppliers with overdue accounts (5), £19M to dissolved-status companies (2), £32M to companies with insolvency history (3). NOTE: Some matches are CH fuzzy-search false positives (e.g. school, government-body name collisions) and need human verification. After verification, real flags = (a) credit-risk review on overdue accounts, (b) contract-cleanup on dissolved entities (records still on ledger but supplier extinct — risk of duplicate-payment leakage), (c) PCR 2015 Reg.57 discretionary exclusion review on insolvency-history suppliers in active contracts.

existing_programme.title: Refund / credit-note management + contract dispute resolution (£200M, 134,517 rows)
existing_programme.rationale: 134,517 negative-amount rows totalling £200M — refunds, credit notes, contract reversals. Volume signals correct ledger capture, but proactive levers exist: (a) contract management review on top recurring refund counterparties, (b) duplicate-payment pre-detection, (c) energy-bill credit-management automation. Typical 5-10% reduction in refund volume + faster reconciliation = 10-30bp net cash improvement.

existing_programme.title: Rebuild general reserves to ≥4 months (Low → Adequate)
existing_programme.rationale: Reserves at 4.6 months (Low per CIPFA Resilience benchmark). Direction: stable. A 4-month minimum is the CIPFA / S151 prudence floor; below this triggers external auditor VFM concern and elevates s.114 risk.

existing_programme.title: Audit + recover £134M in flagged duplicate-payment patterns
existing_programme.rationale: DOGE forensic flagged £134M across 24,976 groups of likely duplicates. Industry recovery norm 5-15% via duplicate-detection software (AP Forensics, FISCAL, Oracle Concur). Lloyds Bank Commercial Card analysis typical for spot-check sample of 100 highest-confidence matches.

existing_programme.title: Investigate £309M in flagged split-payment patterns
existing_programme.rationale: DOGE flagged £309M across 0 split-payment instances. Split payments often indicate (a) below-procurement-threshold ledger fragmentation circumventing PCR 2015 Reg.4 contract-value-aggregation rule; or (b) legitimate sub-line invoice splits. Sample audit + reclassify; misuse triggers Reg. 99 challenge exposure.

additional_opportunities.name: HNSG Local SEND Reform Plan submission — 90% DSG write-off
additional_opportunities.lever_description: Government announced 9 Feb 2026 (alongside final 2026/27 LGFS) that 90% of every English council's accumulated DSG deficit at 31 March 2026 will be written off via a new Section 31 grant — the High Needs Stability Grant (HNSG), worth ~£5.6Bn nationally. Conditional on the council submitting an approved Local SEND Reform Plan to DfE by **19 June 2026**; grants paid Autumn 2026. Safety Valve programme closed 1 April 2026 (folded into HNSG). Statutory override extended to 31 March 2028; gov committed to absorb ALL DSG deficits from 1 April 2028. New 2026/27 + 2027/28 deficits NOT yet covered — linked to demonstrable delivery on approved reform plan (OBR forecast: £8.6Bn additional deficits over those two years).
additional_opportunities.council_specific_rationale: Residual 10% management — plan submission unlocks 90% auto write-off

case_studies.horizon: Autumn 2026 grant; conditional on 19 June 2026 plan submission
case_studies.note: £67.7M deficit → ~£60.9M write-off, ~£6.8M residual. Not previously a Safety Valve participant.
£17M → ~£15.3M write-off, ~£1.7M residual. 2026/27-2028/29 budget approved on HNSG assumption.
Active Safety Valve participant 2022-23 cohort. £17.8M → ~£14.4M HNSG write-off, ~£1.6M residual after SV local contributions count toward 10%.
~£180M at 31 Mar 2026 → ~£162M write-off, ~£18M residual. Not Safety Valve. Reform UK took control 8 May 2026 — plan submission is most material early decision.
